_doc: Known, pre-existing violations of the independent source-anchor oracle
(independent-oracle.ts#checkSourceAnchors), keyed by (fixture, tier).
Why this exists:
checkSourceAnchors re-reads each mapping's claimed (line, column)
against the REAL source file on disk (independent of the source-map
generator and of the committed golden) and flags positions that are
out of bounds, point at whitespace/comments, or split a token in
half. It surfaced real, pre-existing bugs in several tiers' source
location tracking that the byte-identity + structural checks in
run.ts never could, because both of those are graded against the
generator's own output (audit finding #22).
Fixing those generators is out of scope for the change that added
this oracle (conformance/source-map/ only, no compiler edits). This
file pins the CURRENT violation signature per (fixture, tier) so the
independent check can still gate on REGRESSIONS (any drift in
violationCount / trackedCount / totalCount fails until the allowlist
is deliberately updated) without permanently blocking the suite on
known, already-diagnosed issues.
Contract for entries:
- Each entry MUST carry a non-empty `reason` (enforced by
loadKnownIssues — no bare lists).
- `violationCount` / `trackedCount` / `totalCount` are the exact
values from checkSourceAnchors' AnchorReport for that (fixture,
tier) pair against the committed expected-source-map.json golden.
All three are pinned (not just violationCount) so a tier that
regresses from 'partially tracked with N violations' to 'fully
untracked' (as already happened to the Java tier) is still caught
even though its violation *count* wouldn't otherwise change —
checkSourceAnchors treats untracked (line=0) mappings as neither
pass nor violation, only as a trackedCount deficit.
- A (fixture, tier) pair with NO entry here is expected to be fully
clean (0 violations, every mapping position-tracked). Any drift
(new violations, or a pair regressing from clean) fails the gate.
- Entries are removed (not zeroed out) once the underlying generator
bug is fixed, so a clean pair goes back to being unconditionally
enforced rather than silently pinned at violationCount: 0.
F-293 whole-map signature (independent-oracle.ts#checkAgainstReference):
`mergedAnchors` / `extraMappings` pin, per (fixture, tier), how the tier's
map compares to the TS reference map of the same fixture (opcode N is the
same opcode in every tier by hex parity). mergedAnchors = reference
anchors a single tier anchor swallows; extraMappings = opcodes the tier
maps that the reference leaves unmapped (compiler-synthesized). Both
default to 0 when omitted and are matched EXACTLY, so a generator fix
that lands without removing its entry fails, as does a regression.

knownIssues.reason: Rust maps branch-body opcodes (10..26, spanning the then and else bodies and the if condition) onto the single line of the enclosing `if` instead of each body statement, merging 3 reference anchors into one and mapping 6 opcodes the TS reference leaves unmapped. Every mapping is individually valid, so the per-mapping rules cannot see it.
Zig maps 3 opcodes (0, 17, 23) that the TS reference leaves unmapped: the if-branch bookkeeping ops are anchored to the `if` line. Not an anchor-validity defect; pinned so it cannot grow.
